title: decode_body_value: max_bytes=None behavior and truncation contract undocumented
description: mime-tree::decode_body_value() takes max_bytes: Option<usize>. The RFC 8621 §4.1.4 spec uses this for the 'truncated' field in EmailBodyValue. The postconditions callers rely on are not documented: (1) does None mean 'return all bytes' or 'use a crate-defined default limit'? (2) when Some(n) is passed and the decoded body exceeds n bytes, is the output exactly n bytes, or n decoded characters, or n bytes of the pre-decode transfer-encoded form? (3) is the truncated flag in DecodedBodyValue set by this function, and if so, based on what threshold? What goes wrong: a JMAP adapter that passes max_bytes=Some(1024) expecting to get exactly 1024 UTF-8 characters may get 1024 bytes of a multibyte encoding, silently splitting a codepoint. File: mime-tree/src/parse.rs, mime-tree/src/message.rs (DecodedBodyValue.is_truncated field).
